rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This clause explains the command to be patient, or the duty to comply, in light of what the chiefs witnessed of the Prophet's firmness in affirming divine unity.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر بالصبر أو لوجوب الامتثال به والإشارة إلى ما وقع وشاهدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs say Muhammad intends to carry through the grave project of denying their idols' divinity, without being diverted or softened; they should stop hoping to bend him and persist in worshipping their gods.
rows.anchor: أي إن هذا لشيء عظيم يراد من جهته صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم إمضاؤه وتنفيذه لا محالة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes this as a calamity of time intended for them, leaving no recourse but to swallow the bitterness of patience.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الأمر لشيء من نوائب الدهر يراد بنا فلا حيلة إلا تجرع مرارة الصبر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says his call to monotheism, or his pursuit of leadership over Arabs and non-Arabs, is desired by everyone, though not every wish is fulfilled.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن هذا الذي يدعيه من أمر التوحيد أو يقصده من الرياسة والترفع على العرب والعجم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the threatened thing as their own religion, which is being sought so it can be wrested from them and abolished.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أن هذا أي دينكم يطلب لينتزع منكم ويطرح أو يراد إبطاله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes the referent to be patience itself, understood from the command: patience is sought because its outcome is praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الإشارة إلى الصبر المفهوم من ( اصبروا ) أي أن الصبر لشيء مطلوب لأنه محمود العاقبة

rows.speaker: القفال
rows.claim: Al-Qaffal reads the statement as a threat: Muhammad is supposedly not establishing a religion but seeking power to dispose of their wealth and children as he wishes.
rows.anchor: وقال القفال : هذه كلمة تذكر للتهديد والتخويف والمعنى أنه ليس غرضه من هذا القول تقرير الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In “we have not heard of this,” “this” refers to what Muhammad is saying.
rows.anchor: ما سمعنا بهذا ( الذي يقوله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب ومقاتل
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Kaʿb, and Muqatil take the last community to mean the Christians; “last” describes their belief, since they do not accept Muhammad's prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ومجاهد ومحمد بن كعب ومقاتل أرادوا ملة النصارى والتوصيف بالآخرة الإعتقاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the Christian reading, they mean they heard the opposite of monotheism: Christians professed a trinity and claimed it was Jesus' religion, a claim Alusi rejects on Jesus' behalf.
rows.anchor: ومرادهم من قولهم ما سمعنا الخ أنا سمعنا خلافه وهو عدم التوحيد فإن النصارى كانوا يثلثون

rows.speaker: مجاهد وقتادة
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada also take the phrase to mean the Arabs' religion and custom, inherited from their fathers.
rows.anchor: وعن مجاهد أيضا وقتادة أرادوا ملة العرب ونحلتها التي أدركوا عليها آباءهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parsing makes “in the last community” circumstantial from the demonstrative “this,” rather than governed by “we heard”; the claim then concerns the end-time community's monotheistic religion.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون في الملة الآخرة حالا من اسصم الإشارة لا متعلقا بسمعنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that parsing, they claim scripture people and soothsayers had not foretold a monotheist end-time prophet; Alusi says this is a lie, since his idol-breaking call to worship God was widely known before his appearance.
rows.anchor: ولقد كذبوا في ذلك فإن حديث إن النبي المبعوث آخر الزمان يكسر الأصنام ويدعو إلى توحيد الملك العلام كان أشهر الأمور قبل الظهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Fabrication” means an invention and falsehood with no precedent or model.
rows.anchor: أي افتعال وافتراء من غير سبق مثل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the discussion and explains why remembrance is specially received by people of understanding.
rows.anchor: استئناف جلر مجرى التعليل لما قبله من تخصيص الذكرى بأولي الألباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Expansion” literally means spreading or extending flesh; figuratively it means capaciousness, and here God's creation of the rational soul with complete readiness to accept Islam.
rows.anchor: الشرح في الأصل البسط والمد للحم ونحوه ويكنى به عن التسويع وتجوز به هنا عن خلق النفس الناطقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chest stands for the rational soul by way of the heart in which it first attaches through a subtle vapor from refined nourishment, then governs and directs the body; this soul bears Islam and faith.
rows.anchor: من حيث أنه محل للقلب وفي تجويفه بخار لطيف يتكون من صفوة الأغذية وبه تتعلق النفس أولا

rows.speaker: بعض الأجلة
rows.claim: Some eminent scholars classify “God expanded his chest” as a representational metaphor.
rows.anchor: وجعل بعض الأجلة شرح الله صدره استعارة تمثيلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative hamza denies an omitted premise; the fa coordinates to that premise and the predicate of “who” is omitted but supplied by what follows: are all people equal?
rows.anchor: لدلالة ما بعده عليه والتقدير أكل الناس سواء فمن شرح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The expanded person was created ready for Islam and remains upon original human disposition, unchanged by acquired corrupting influences.
rows.anchor: وخلقه مستعدا للإسلام فبقي على الفطرة الأصلية ولم تتغير بالعوارض المكتسبة القادحة فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The light is God's grace shining from the towers of mercy, enabling him to recognize the signs in creation and revelation and follow them to truth.
rows.anchor: وهو اللطف الإلهي المشرق عليه من بروج الرحمة عند مشاهدة الآيات التكوينية والتنزيلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi also allows that the light may be a divine reality distinct from grace and enabling guidance, by which truth is apprehended.
rows.anchor: وقد يقال : هو أمر إلهي غير اللطف والتوفيق يدرك به الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By bad choice, the opposite person replaces God's original disposition, hardens the heart, constricts the chest, falls under error's darkness, and turns wholly away from signs without remembering or benefiting from them.
rows.anchor: كمن قسا قلبه وحرج صدره بتبديل فطرة الله تعالى بسوء اختياره وستولى عليه ظلمات الغي والضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording “upon a light” rather than “has a light” depicts continued, settled residence in light, a metaphor for grace and guidance.
rows.anchor: للدلالة على استمرار ذلك واستقراره في النور وهو مستعار للطف والتوفيق للإهتداء

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet explained an expanded heart as one into which light enters and which then opens; its signs are longing for the eternal home, detachment from the delusive world, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: وجاء برواية الثعلبي في تفسيره والحاكم في مستدركه والبيهقي في شعب الإيمان وابن مردويه عن ابن مسعود أنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi resolves the report's apparent reversal of the verse's order by distinguishing innate readiness in the verse from later expansion after grace in the report; guidance has prior and later stages, and the answer uses the wise redirection of a question.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن السؤال عما في الآية وأن الجواب بيان لكيفيته وأجيب بأن الإهتداء له مراتب بعضها مقدم وبعضها مؤخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Because of God's remembrance” means that mentioning God or His signs should soften hearts, but these people recoil and grow harder.
rows.anchor: أي من أجل ذكره سبحانه الذي حقه أن تلين منه القلوب أي إذا ذكر الله تعالى عندهم أو آياته عز وجل اشمأزوا من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads “away from God's remembrance”; the transmitted “because of” is stronger, since those hardened because of it resist acceptance more than those hardened for another reason.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( عن ذكر الله ) والمتواترة أبلغ لأن القاسي من أجل الشيء أشد تأبيا من قبوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning chest expansion for believers and heart-hardness for rejecters intensifies the contrast: the believer's acceptance overflows the heart to fill the chest, while the hard heart admits nothing.
rows.anchor: ذكر شرح الصدر لأن توسعته وجعله محلا للإسلام دون القلب الذي فيه يدل على شدته وإفراط كثرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attributing expansion to God signals its fullest form, as the act of an omnipotent, wise agent.
rows.anchor: وإسناده إلى الله تعالى الظاهر في أنه على أتم الوجوه لأنه فعل قادر حكيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The counterpart is hardness rather than tightness: like a solid rock, hardness accepts nothing, whereas tightness suggests accepting at least a little.
rows.anchor: وقابله بالقساوة مع أن مقتضى المقابلة أن يعبر بالضيق لأن القساوة كما في الصخرة الصماء تقتضي عدم قبول شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text does not explicitly attribute their hardness to God's making it, implying that it clings so deeply it would arise from their own natures even without being created.
rows.anchor: وعدل عن التعبير بما يفيد مجعولية القساوة له تعالى وخلقه إياها للإشارة إلى غاية لزومها لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardness is assigned to hearts rather than chests because the heart is the organ whose corruption corrupts the whole body.
rows.anchor: وأما إسنادها إلى القلوب دون الصدور فللتنصيص على فساد هذا العضو الذي إذا فسد فسد الجسد كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believer is singular but the unbelievers plural to suggest that believers, though many, are like one person, unlike the unbelievers.
rows.anchor: للإشارة إلى أن المؤمنين وأن تعددوا كرجل واحد ولا كذلك الكفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those” points to the distant ones characterized by hard hearts, who are in manifest error.
rows.anchor: أولئك ( البعداء المتصفون بما ذكر من قسوة القلوب ( في ضلال مبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the verse was revealed about Ali and Hamza, whose chests God expanded for Islam, and Abu Lahab and his son, whose hearts were hard.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت في علي وحمزة رضي الله تعالى عنهما وأبي لهب وابنه فعلي كرم الله تعالى وجهه وحمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best discourse is the noble Quran.
rows.anchor: هو القرآن الكريم وكونه حديثا بمعنى كونه كلاما محدثا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the Quran hadith means discourse that is spoken of, not speech newly created in opposition to the eternal.
rows.anchor: وكونه حديثا بمعنى كونه كلاما محدثا به لا بمعنى كونه مقابلا للقديم

rows.speaker: الأشاعرة
rows.claim: Asharites who hold that verbal speech is created and necessarily linked to the eternal apply descriptions implying createdness to that verbal speech.
rows.anchor: ومن قال بالتلازم من الأشاعرة القائلين بحدوث الكلام اللفظي جعل الأوصاف الدالة على الحدوث لذلك الكلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi also allows “hadith” to be applied to the Quran by way of matching expression, or mushakala.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون إطلاق الحديث هنا على القرآن من باب المشاكلة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that some Companions asked the Prophet for beautiful stories and accounts of earlier times, after which this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن قوما من الصحابة قالوا : يا رسول الله حدثنا بأحاديث حسان وبأخبار الدهر فنزلت

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Companions tired of admonition and asked the Prophet to tell them something; the verse directed them to fresh recitation and listening to the Quran.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن مسعود أن الصحابة ملوا ملة فقالوا له عليه الصلاة والسلام حدثنا فنزلت أي إراشادا لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Making God's name the subject and “revealed” its predicate magnifies the Quran, attests its excellence and divine source, and emphasizes that no one else could produce its like.
rows.anchor: وفي إيقاع اسم الله تعالى مبتدأ وبناء ( نزل ) عليه تفخيم لأحسن الحديث واستشهاد على أحسنيته وتأكيد لاستناده إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God is unsurpassed in perfection, nothing else has comparable perfection; the most perfect discourse must necessarily come from the most perfect speaker.
rows.anchor: لأن أكمل الحديث إنما يكون من أكمل متكلم ضرورة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says this construction conveys exclusivity, which he sees as compatible with reverent awareness.
rows.anchor: مذهب الزمخشري أن مثل هذا التركيب يفيد الحصر وأنه لا تنافي بينه وبين التقوى جمعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “A book” may be apposition to “the best discourse” or a circumstantial accusative, as al-Zamakhshari allows.
rows.anchor: كتابا ( بدل من ( أحسن الحديث ) أو حال منه كما قال الزمخشري

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Alusi rejects Abu Hayyan's assumption that the circumstantial reading depends on the comparative's genitive making it definite; any genitive construction suffices.
rows.anchor: وليس مبنيا على القول بأن إضافة أفعل التفضيل تفيده تعريفا كما ظن أبو حيان فإن مطلق الإضافة كافية في صحة الحالية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun can function circumstantially because it is qualified by “mutashabih,” or because it carries the force of “written.”
rows.anchor: ووقوعه حالا مع كونه اسما لا صفة إما لوصفه بقوله تعالى ( متشابها ( أو لكونه في قوة مكتوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's meanings resemble one another in soundness, precision, truth, benefit in worldly and afterlife affairs, while its eloquent wording and arrangement mutually echo inimitably.
rows.anchor: والمراد بكونه متشابها هنا معانيه في الصحة والإحكام والإبتناء على الحق والصدق واستتباع منافع الخلق في المعاد والمعاش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi likens this mutual excellence to the Arab description of a perfectly beautiful face as “mutanasif,” as though each part were evenly fair.
rows.anchor: وما أشبه هذا بقول العرب في الوجه الكامل حسنا وجه متناصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mathani” is another adjective or circumstantial qualifier for the book; as an irregular plural of muthanna, it means repeated in rulings, exhortations, and stories.
rows.anchor: ( مثاني ( صفة أخرى لكتابا أو حال أخرى منه وهو جمع مثنى بضم الميم وفتح النون المشددة على خلاف القياس

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the Quran is called “mathani” because it is repeated in recitation.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لأنه يثنى في التلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Mathani” may be a plural of muthanna, from duality as repetition: a turn after a turn; the dual is itself the first degree of repetition and may be pluralized for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون جمع مثنى بالفتح مخففا من التثنية بمعنى التكرير والإعادة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another derivation is from praise: the verses contain praise of God or, through their eloquence and inimitability, praise their speaker; Alusi finds this less fitting beside “mutashabih” unless the latter sense is intended.
rows.anchor: وقيل : جمع لاشتمال آياته على الثناء على الله تعالى أو لأنها تثنى ببلاغتها وإعجازها على المتكلم بها

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf finds the form best derived from praise or repetition: muthanna can be a verbal noun made adjectival, or a noun transferred to an adjective for emphasis, like a land of predators.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف إلا قيس بحسب اللفظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As an adjective for the book, “mathani” describes its details, which constitute the whole: the Quran is composed of portions, chapters, verses, rulings, admonitions, and stories.
rows.anchor: ووقوعه صفة لكتاب باعتبار تفاصيله وتفاصيل الشيء هي جملته لا غير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may instead be an accusative of specification transformed from the subject: the underlying construction is “its details resemble one another”; it is indefinite by the usual pattern.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون تمييزا محولا عن الفاعل والأصل متشابها مثانيه فحول ونكر لأن الأكثر التنكير

rows.speaker: هشام وأبو بشر
rows.claim: Hisham and Abu Bishr read “mathani” with a quiescent ya, either as the predicate of an omitted subject or as an accusative with ya quiescence from a dialect that drops its vowel.
rows.anchor: وقرأ هشام وأبو بشر ( مثاني ) بسكون الياء فاحتمل أن يكون خبر مبتدأ محذوف

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Some parse “the skins shiver” as an adjective or circumstantial clause for the book, which already has a qualifying description.
rows.anchor: قيل صفة لكتابا أو حال منه لتخصصه بالصفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi prefers to start a new sentence here: it describes the Quran's visible effects on its listeners after describing the book itself and confirms its excellence.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض : الأظهر أنه استئناف مسوق لبيان آثاره الظاهرة في سامعيه بعد بيان أوصافه في نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qashʿarīrah is severe contraction; the word derives from qashʿ, dry hide, with an added ra to form a quadriliteral and signal extra meaning, as skin contracts and hair stands from sudden fear.
rows.anchor: وأقشعرار التقبض يقال اقشعر الجلد إذا تقبض تقبضا شديدا وتركيبه من القشع وهو الأديم اليابس قد ضم إليه الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description pictures the believers' fear by naming its tangible bodily signs; Alusi calls this figurative exemplification, even if it also operates through metonymy.
rows.anchor: والمراد تصوير خوفهم بذكر لوازمه المحسوسة ويطلق عليه التمثيل وإن كان من باب الكناية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi records an alternative calling the description a true parable that compares one state with another; he prefers the account that figures fear through its tangible effects because the story-to-story metaphor is strained.
rows.anchor: هو تصوير للخوف بذكر آثاره وتشبيه حالة بحالة فيكون تمثيلا حقيقة والأول أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi takes the bodily change as actually occurring: warning verses make hearers fear and their skins shiver; hearing promises of mercy turns fear into hope and dread into longing.
rows.anchor: بيان حصول تلك الحالة وعروضها لهم بطريق التحقيق والمعنى أنهم إذا سمعوا القرآن

words: ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their skins and hearts then become quiet and settled through remembrance of God's mercy, which is unstated because mercy is the first thing that comes to mind when God is mentioned.
rows.anchor: أي ساكنة مطمئنة إلى ذكر رحمته تعالى وإنما لم يصرح بالرحمة إيذانا بأنها أول ما يخطر بالبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied mercy is supported by the report, “My mercy preceded My anger.”
rows.anchor: كما يرشد إليه خبر سبقت رحمتي غضبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He mentions hearts with the softening because fear belongs to the heart and hearts can soften, while skin shivering cannot be predicated of hearts.
rows.anchor: وذكر القلوب لتقدم الخشية التي هي من عوارضها ولعله إنما لم تذكر هناك على طرز ذكرها هنا لأنها لا توصف بالإقشعرار وتوصف باللين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn Urwa asked his grandmother Asma how the Prophet's Companions behaved when reciting Quran; she said their eyes wept and skins shivered as described, and she sought God's protection from Satan when told some people fainted.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عروة بن الزبير قال : قلت لجدتي أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes shivering and subsequent calm; it does not describe swooning, ecstatic display, or clapping, which Alusi condemns in some practitioners.
rows.anchor: وليس في الآية أكثر من نعت أوليائه باقشعرار الجلود من القرآن ثم سكونهم إلى رحمته عز وجل وليس فيها نعتهم بالصعق والتواجد والصفق

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن الزبير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Zubayr told his mother Asma that people remembering God trembled and fainted; she told him not to sit with them and asked whether they thought themselves more fearful than the Prophet, Abu Bakr, and Umar, whom she had seen recite without this.
rows.anchor: عن عامر عن عبد الله بن الزبير قال : جئت أمي فقلت وجدت قوما

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar, seeing someone collapse while hearing Quran, said that they fear God without collapsing and that Satan enters such people.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عمر وقد رأى ساقطا من سماع القرآن فقال إنا لنخشى الله تعالى وما نسقط : هؤلاء

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada calls this the description of God's allies: their skins shiver, eyes weep, and hearts find rest in remembrance; God does not describe them as losing reason or fainting, which he associates with innovators and Satan.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة أنه قال في الآية هذا نعت أولياء الله تعالى قال : تقشعر جلودهم وتبكي أعينهم

rows.speaker: ابن جبير
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says swooning is from Satan.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جبير : قال الصعقة من الشيطان

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin proposes testing people who faint at Quran recitation by seating one against a wall with legs extended and reading the whole Quran; if he throws himself down, he is truthful.
rows.anchor: قال ابن سيرين : بيننا وبين هؤلاء الذين يصرعون عند قراءة القرآن أن يحمل أحدهم على حائط باسطا رجليه

rows.speaker: مشايخهم
rows.claim: Some Sufi shaykhs explain swooning as weak hearts unable to bear spiritual influx; Alusi counters that it signals deficiency, since a completed wayfarer grows firm and strong like the Companions.
rows.anchor: ويقول مشايخهم : إن ذلك لضعف القلوب عن تحمل الوارد وليس فاعلو ذلك في الكمال كالصحابة أهل الصدر الأول

rows.speaker: مشايخهم
rows.claim: The Sufi defense says the verse affirms shivering and softening without excluding other states, and its relative clause describes firmly established saints rather than every believer.
rows.anchor: ويقولون : ليس في الآية أكثر من إثبات الإقشعرار واللين وليس فيها نفي أن يعتريهم حال آخر بل في الآية إشعار بأن المذكور حال الراسخين الكاملين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative clause indicates people deeply established in recognizable fear, so the description need not be exclusive or define others' states; involuntary reactions like sneezing need no blame, as Ibn Sirin's remark supports, and Alusi prays for the Companions' grace.
rows.anchor: ومقتضى معلومية الصلة أن لهم رسوخا في الخشية حتى يعلموا بها فلا يلزم من كون حالهم ما ذكر ليس إلا على فرض دلالتها على الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” points to the Quran whose qualities were just described; God guides by it whom He wills by enabling reflection on its proofs of truth and divine origin.
rows.anchor: شواهد الحقية ودلائل كونه من عنده عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi also considers making the pronoun in “wills” refer to the person: God guides whoever wills God's guidance, but he finds this reading weak.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ضمير ( يشاء ) لمن والمعنى يهدي الله تعالى من يشاء هداية الله تعالى وليس بذاك

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God creates misguidance in the person as he turns away from what directs him to truth through a bad disposition; no guide can rescue him from error.
rows.anchor: أي يخلق سبحانه فيه الضلال إعراضه عما يرشده إلى الحق بسوء استعداده فما له من هاد

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes “that” to mean the shivering and softening just described, whose effect is guidance; whoever is unaffected because of hardness and persistent sin has no guide able to influence him. Alusi dismisses this reading.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الإشارة إلى المذكور من الإقشعرار واللين والمعنى ذلك الذي ذكر من الخشية والرجاء أثر هداه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse resumes the argument to explain the contrast between the guided and the astray.
rows.anchor: استئناف جار مجرى التعليل لما قبله من تباين حال المهتدي والضال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted premise is “are all people equal?”: is the person forced to ward off punishment with his face like one safe from harm and in no need of protection?
rows.anchor: التقدير أكل الناس سواء فمن شأنه أن يتقي بوجهه الذي هو أشرف أعضائه يوم القيامة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face is literal: his hand, which once warded off harms, is chained to his neck, leaving him to shield himself with his most honored limb.
rows.anchor: فالوجه على حقيقته وقد يحمل على ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without the report that the hand is chained, taking the face literally vividly depicts the completeness and earnestness of his self-protection.
rows.anchor: وقد يحمل على ذلك من غير حاجة إلى حديث كون اليد مغلولة تصويرا لكمال اتقائه وجده فيه وهو أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The face may mean the whole person, making the image hyperbolic.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الوجه بمعنى الجملة والمبالغة عليه دون المبالغة فيما قبله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view treats face-protection as a figure for having no shield at all, since the face is not a means of protection; Alusi finds this strained.
rows.anchor: وقيل الإتقاء بالوجه كناية عن عدم ما يتقى به إذ الإتقاء بالوجه لا وجه له لأنه لا يتقي به ولا يخلو عن خدش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “On the Day of Resurrection” may be governed by “protects himself,” or attached to “the evil of punishment,” meaning the punishment of that Day; Alusi calls the latter sound but the former more immediate.
rows.anchor: معمول يتقي كما أشرنا إلى ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited line depicts the literal face and chest meeting swords, with the head serving as a helmet.
rows.anchor: يلقى السيوف بوجهه وبنحره ويقيم هامته مقام المغفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alusi says the verse was revealed about Abu Jahl.
rows.anchor: والآية نزلت في أبي جهل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “It was said to the wrongdoers” may coordinate with “protects himself”; the past tense signals certainty. Alternatively, it is a circumstantial clause, with or without an implied “already.”
rows.anchor: عطف على يتقي أي ويقال لهم من جهة خزنة النار وصيغة الماضي للدلالة على التحقق والتقرر وقيل الواو للحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit noun “wrongdoers” replaces a pronoun to condemn them and signal why they are told to taste punishment.
rows.anchor: ووضع المظهر موضع المضمر للتسجيل عليهم بالظلم والإشعار بعلة الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are commanded to taste the continuing consequence of their worldly earnings in disbelief and sins.
rows.anchor: أي وبال ما كنتم تكسبون في الدنيا على الدوام من الكفر والمعاصي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative emphatically denies that God fails to suffice His servant: the certainty of His sufficiency is so clear none can deny or hesitate over it.
rows.anchor: إنكار ونفي لعدم كفايته تعالى على أبلغ وجه كأن الكفاية من التحقق والظهور بحيث لا يقدر أحد على أن يتفوه بعدمها

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says “His servant” means the Messenger; the following threat by those besides God supports this, since the Quraysh refer to their idols.
rows.anchor: على ما روي عن السدي وأيد

rows.speaker: قريش
rows.claim: The Quraysh warned the Prophet that their idols might drive him mad or harm him for disparaging them; another report has them demanding he stop insulting their gods or suffer harm, after which the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: وقد روي أن قريشا قالت له عليه الصلاة والسلام : إنا نخاف أن تخبلك آلهتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “His servant” is generic, with the Prophet included foremost; the plural reading supports this and is interpreted as covering prophets and believers.
rows.anchor: أو الجنس المنتظم له عليه الصلاة والسلام انتضاما أوليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the singular reading, followers are also intended: God suffices the Prophet and believers in the necessities of religion and worldly life and protects them from unbelievers.
rows.anchor: ومن أنه داخل في كفاية مهمي الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام وأتباعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage connects the denunciation of those who lie about God and deny truth with the recompense of the truthful believer, then extends God's favor to His servant.
rows.anchor: لدلالته على أنه تعالى يكفي نبيه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم مهم دينه ودنياه

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر ومجاهد وابن وثاب وطلحة والأعمش وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Abu Jafar, Mujahid, Ibn Waththab, Talha, al-Amash, Hamza, and al-Kisai read “His servants” in the plural; other readings make it genitive after “sufficing” or use the verb “yukafi” with an accusative object.
rows.anchor: وقريء ( بكافي عباده ) بالإضافة و ( يكافي عباده ) مضارع كافي ونصب ( عباده )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “yukafi” reading may derive from sufficiency, like “yujari” for “yajri,” and be more emphatic through its intensive form; Alusi finds this likely given the Quran's frequent use of that sense.
rows.anchor: وهو أبلغ من كفى لبنائه على لفظ المبالغة وهو الظاهر لكثرة تردد هذا المعنى في القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternate form may instead be hamzated and derive from mukafaah, meaning requital.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون مهموزا من المكافأة وهي المجازاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requital reading fits the preceding rewards and the Prophet's focus: God will surely recompense His beloved servant, while the idol-threats warn of a supposed counter-recompense; still, the common reading's meaning of sufficiency is stronger.
rows.anchor: نعم لا ننكر أن معنى الكفاية أبلغ كما هو مقتضى القراءة المشهورة

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God misguides becomes heedless of His sufficiency for His servant and fears things that cannot benefit or harm; such a person has no guide to lead him to good.
rows.anchor: لا ينفع ولا يضر أصلا
